A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scLDM research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Reporting inconsistencies in v2 limit interpretation of particular results but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction, conditional and unconditional generation, perturbation prediction, classification and ablation results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds pooling comparisons, likelihood comparisons, gene-level diagnostics and computational resource measurements.

M1.justification: V2 explicitly instantiates a Gaussian observation head alongside the Negative Binomial decoder, adding a mean-output Gaussian layer to Table 8 and evaluating both variants. Gaussian likelihoods were already contemplated in v1, making this a limited variant extension. MCAB, two-stage training and joint guidance remain unchanged; expressed-gene filtering moves from v1 Appendix F.1 into the main text.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same observational datasets, Parse1M and Replogle perturbation datasets, Census training data, and COVID-19 and Tabula Sapiens classification tasks. The held-out biological contexts remain unchanged. Added diagnostics and analyses use this retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds CellFlow, previously only cited, to the central perturbational generation and cell-eval comparisons. It also introduces direct comparisons against max-, mean- and sum-pooling substitutes for MCAB in Figure 5. These substantially expand the relevant comparison methods; STATE and STATE-Tx denote the retained baseline.

E3.justification: V2 expands evaluation with leave-one-out 1-NN accuracy, k-NN precision/recall with k=3, and gene-level R2 metrics. Appendix K.7 introduces generation evaluation directly in gene space for perturbations with more than 10 Wilcoxon-identified DEGs. Attention analysis increases its stated sample from 1,000 to 2,500 cells, and Gaussian configurations are newly evaluated. Existing biological holdouts and classification protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds aggregation and likelihood comparisons, diagnostics of gene means, variances and sparsity, and DEG-focused generation analysis. Attention-enrichment analyses extend from Dentate Gyrus to Tabula Muris and HLCA. The earlier zero-filtering, architectural scaling and guidance studies remain; the guidance-weight results in v2 Table 21 were already present in v1 Table 3.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly identifies Table 1 uncertainties as standard errors and reports standard deviations across three random seeds for the new pooling ablation. Training-time measurements also identify their uncertainties as standard errors across runs. The existing three-generation-seed protocol and distinction between scLDM sampling seeds and baseline retraining seeds are retained; no increase in those run counts is established.

E6.justification: Reconstruction and generation scores are extensively revised: Table 1 changes scLDM reconstruction error from 5232.9 to 4571.6 on Dentate Gyrus and from 4102.1 to 4898.9 on HLCA. New CellFlow results have lower W2 than both scLDM variants on both perturbational datasets. R2 and DEG results are added, while classification scores remain unchanged. V2 Table 16 duplicates its Dentate Gyrus and Tabula Muris blocks, limiting interpretation of those reported revisions.

T1.justification: V2 adds explicit mathematical definitions of the gene-level mean, variance and zero-count R2 assessments and formalizes the alternative aggregation mappings in Appendix K.1. The core ELBO formulation, guidance equations, attention Properties 1-4 and their proofs are retained; there is no new central theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal architecture and generation contributions remain substantially unchanged. V2's introduction adds an explicit claim that gene-index embeddings permit vocabulary flexibility across tissues or species without retraining. Its conclusion removes v1's stronger assertion that enforcing exchangeability is crucial, and the contribution list makes the joint-versus-additive guidance comparison explicit.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations that encoder filtering preserves the decoder's ability to model zeros and that the 2,000-gene restriction reflects the evaluation protocol. It interprets generation through precision/recall tradeoffs and adds limitations concerning task-dependent likelihood selection and transcriptomic-only modeling. V1's specific warning about deceptively favorable sparse-data metrics for scDiffusion is replaced by a more general evaluation caveat.

D1.justification: New Tables 12-14 disclose dataset-specific parameter counts, FLOPs, training times, peak memory and eight-A100 hardware, distinguishing measured times from single-GPU projections. V2 also specifies CellFlow's PCA representation and 500,000-step training, the Gaussian output head, and pooling-comparator implementation. These materially expand reproducibility information. The code link already existed in v1 and is relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for Connell's single-cell language model and scVAEDer, plus references supporting the new evaluation metrics. It clarifies MCAB's relationship to Perceiver IO and distinguishes its gene-indexed decoder queries from earlier set architectures. The broader research positioning remains intact; citation-style and publication-metadata changes do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: Most of the narrative and section sequence are retained. V2 moves input processing into Section 3.2 and the code disclosure into the introduction, locally rewrites contributions and results discussions, and adds Limitations and Impact Statement sections. Author affiliations and correspondence information change, while the author-contribution section is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout and substantially compresses the principal results tables and figures. Tables gain likelihood variants and metric columns; computational-cost and diagnostic tables are added. Attention heatmaps are redrawn with different color-scale ranges and extended to additional retained datasets, and a pooling-ablation figure is added. Existing guidance-weight results are separated into an appendix table.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evidence missing from v1 through the CellFlow comparison, controlled pooling analysis, likelihood and gene-level diagnostics, and explicit resource reporting and limitations. However, Table 16 duplicates dataset blocks and conflicts with its accompanying gene-selection description, while Tables 3 and 21 report unexplained different NB results at guidance weight 1. These reporting problems and the compressed main-table typography limit the overall benefit.
